findings.evidence: Every ideal-dependent step in lines 89–98 is already parameterized by the chosen ideal (`map_mk_X_sub_C hc`, `IsWeierstrassDivisorAt I`, and `isWeierstrassDivisionAt_div_mod`); Mathlib declares the latter at `WeierstrassPreparation.lean:298` with `[IsAdicComplete I A]`, without a local-ring assumption.
findings.fix: Prove the theorem first with `{I : Ideal A} [IsAdicComplete I A] (hc : c ∈ I)`, replacing each `maximalIdeal A` by `I`; derive the local-ring version only if useful.
findings.issue: `X_sub_C_dvd_iff_aeval_eq_zero` unnecessarily assumes `[IsLocalRing A]` and completion at `maximalIdeal A`, although the argument only needs an ideal `I`, `c ∈ I`, and `[IsAdicComplete I A]`.

summary: The linear-factor criterion is unnecessarily restricted to maximal-ideal completions of local rings; its proof and Mathlib’s division theorem work for any ideal.
